title: Top-K Min Stack
description:
Design a stack `TopKMinStack` that supports standard LIFO push/pop, full-stack minimum (`getMin`), and **top-`k` minimum queries (`getTopKMin(k)`)** returning the minimum among the `k` most recently pushed elements currently on the stack — with `O(log n)` `push` and **`O(1)` `pop`, `getMin`, and `getTopKMin`**!

Implement the `TopKMinStack` class:
- `TopKMinStack()` initializes an empty stack.
- `void push(int val)` pushes `val` onto the top of the stack.
- `int pop()` removes and returns the top element of the stack.
- `int getMin()` returns the minimum element across the entire stack.
- `int getTopKMin(int k)` returns the minimum among the top `k` elements (`1 <= k <= currentSize`).
constraints: Methods pop and getMin are always called on non-empty stacks, and getTopKMin(k) always satisfies 1 <= k <= currentSize.
At most 2 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Maintain a dynamic sparse table on the stack: for each stack position `i`, store `up[i][j]` = minimum of the `2^j` elements ending at index `i` (`2^j <= i + 1`).

On `push(val)` compute `up[i][j] = min(up[i][j-1], up[i - 2^(j-1)][j-1])` in O(log n); on `pop()` simply remove the last row in O(1); on `getTopKMin(k)`, let `p = floor(log2(k))` and return `min(up[n-1][p], up[n - k + 2^p - 1][p])` in O(1).

examples.explanation: Stack [1, 5, 3, 7]: top-1 min is 7, top-2 min is min(3,7)=3, top-3 min is min(5,3,7)=3, top-4/getMin is 1.
After popping 2 from [8, 4, 9, 2], stack is [8, 4, 9] so top-2 min is 4 and top-1 min is 9.
Single element -5 has getTopKMin(1) = -5 and getMin() = -5.
